links.outcome: Accuracy of automated external monitor detecting user self-harm/harm-to-others risk in chatbot conversations versus human consensus
links.effect: User self-harm detection was perfect (accuracy 1.00, sensitivity 1.00, kappa 1.00) including subtle cases; high-risk categories had errors in only 9/100 transcripts (7 false negatives).
links.quote: Notably, ASTRA had perfect agreement with expert human ratings on user indications of self-harm.

links.outcome: Detection of AI therapist failures to respond appropriately to self-harm or harm-to-others disclosures, with false negatives and positives
links.effect: Therapist self-harm response failures: sensitivity 0.74, specificity 1.00 (combined); therapist other-harm sensitivity 0.93; 16/100 transcripts had at least 1 false negative.
links.quote: Across all tasks, 22% (22/100) of transcripts contained at least 1 error, including 7% (7/100) with at least 1 false positive and 16% (16/100) with at least 1 false negative.

links.outcome: Automated detection of inappropriate AI therapist language (flirting, rude or repetitive remarks) versus human ratings
links.effect: Therapist flirting sensitivity 0.94, kappa 0.96; therapist rude/inappropriate remarks sensitivity 0.68, accuracy 0.91, kappa 0.74 (combined).
links.quote: ASTRA’s lowest accuracy (0.90-0.92) occurred when detecting rude, repetitive, or otherwise inappropriate remarks from the AI therapist.

links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM safety classifier outputs across prompt iterations and repeated runs
links.effect: Iteration 2 showed reduced sensitivity for some categories (therapist rude 0.79 to 0.55); authors note LLM may not replicate outputs and differences may be probabilistic artifact; single run at temperature 1.0.
links.quote: Additionally, LLMs may not replicate their own outputs, so differences between prompt iterations may be a probabilistic artifact.
